name: 21s Curl
equipmentNotes: A barbell, run as seven half reps low, seven high, seven full.

name: 45-Degree Back Extension
equipmentNotes: Requires a dedicated 45-degree hyperextension bench (Roman chair) with angled hip pad and ankle/foot lever; distinct from flat back-extension benches and 90-degree reverse-hyper machines. Often progressed with a held dumbbell, plate, or barbell across the back.

name: 90/90 Hip Switch
equipmentNotes: Floor space to sit with both knees bent at right angles.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
equipmentNotes: An ab wheel and floor space; a pad for the knees.

name: Active Hang
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar with room to hang at full stretch.

name: Alternating Dumbbell Curl
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells, curled one arm at a time.

name: Anderson Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a power or squat rack with safety pins/arms adjustable down to bottom squat depth so the bar can be unracked/paused from a dead stop at full depth.

name: Ankle Rocking
equipmentNotes: A wall to measure against and a pad for the down knee; the heel stays down as the knee travels over the toes.

name: Approach Jump
equipmentNotes: A short run-up and overhead clearance.

name: Archer Push-Up
equipmentNotes: Floor space; one arm straight out to the side each rep.

name: Arnold Press
equipmentNotes: Dumbbells and a bench with an upright back, or done standing.

name: Assisted Dip
equipmentNotes: An assisted dip machine or a band across the bars. The number set is assistance, not load.

name: Assisted Pull-Up
equipmentNotes: An assisted pull-up machine. The stack sets assistance, not load, so its number moves opposite to strength and no ratio against a pull-up is meaningful.

name: Back Extension
equipmentNotes: Requires a dedicated back-extension bench or Roman chair (fixed ~45°/90° or adjustable) with hip/thigh pad and ankle/heel brace, allowing free hip hinge below the pad. A flat bench with a partner anchoring the ankles is a common improvisation. No rack, safeties, or bar hooks needed.

name: Back Extension Machine
equipmentNotes: A seated back extension machine with a back pad and a thigh restraint.

name: Back Squat
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a rack with safeties set below depth.

name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar and a looped resistance band. The band unloads the bottom of the rep, so no ratio against a pull-up is meaningful.

name: Band Chest Press
equipmentNotes: A resistance band anchored behind at chest height. A band's resistance changes with how far it is stretched and differs by brand, so no load ratio against a free-weight lift is meaningful.

name: Band Face Pull
equipmentNotes: A resistance band anchored at face height. A band's resistance changes with how far it is stretched and differs by brand, so no load ratio against a free-weight lift is meaningful.

name: Band Good Morning
equipmentNotes: A resistance band stood on and looped behind the neck. A band's resistance changes with how far it is stretched and differs by brand, so no load ratio against a free-weight lift is meaningful.

name: Band Lateral Raise
equipmentNotes: A resistance band stood on and held at the sides. A band's resistance changes with how far it is stretched and differs by brand, so no load ratio against a free-weight lift is meaningful.

name: Band Neck Extension
equipmentNotes: A band anchored at eye level (or underfoot) and looped behind the head; move the head back from flexion into extension against the band.

name: Band Pull-Apart
equipmentNotes: A light resistance band held at shoulder width.

name: Band Pull-Through
equipmentNotes: A resistance band anchored low behind, pulled through between the legs. A band's resistance changes with how far it is stretched and differs by brand, so no load ratio against a free-weight lift is meaningful.

name: Band-Resisted Sprint
equipmentNotes: A long resistance band and a partner or anchor; a lane to run.

name: Band Row
equipmentNotes: A resistance band anchored ahead at waist height, or looped around the feet. A band's resistance changes with how far it is stretched and differs by brand, so no load ratio against a free-weight lift is meaningful.

name: Banded Squat
equipmentNotes: A resistance band stood on and held at the shoulders. A band's resistance changes with how far it is stretched and differs by brand, so no load ratio against a free-weight lift is meaningful.

name: Barbell Bench Press
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a flat bench in a rack with safeties.

name: Barbell Curl
equipmentNotes: A straight barbell.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
equipmentNotes: Requires a barbell pad for hip/groin comfort, clear floor space to lie flat with knees bent and feet flat, and weight plates for loading. No bench, rack, or safety arms needed.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
equipmentNotes: Requires a flat stable bench for upper-back support, a barbell pad across the hip crease, and clear floor space in front of the bench; no squat rack/safeties needed.

name: Barbell Lunge
equipmentNotes: A barbell on the back and room to step.

name: Barbell Rollout
equipmentNotes: A barbell with round plates that will roll, and a pad for the knees.

name: Barbell Row
equipmentNotes: A barbell and room to hinge over it.

name: Barbell Shrug
equipmentNotes: A barbell, or a rack to take it from.

name: Barbell Wrist Curl
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a bench to rest the forearms on.

name: Bayesian Cable Curl
equipmentNotes: A low cable pulley with a single handle, stood forward of the stack so the arm trails behind.

name: Bear Crawl
equipmentNotes: Open floor to travel across.

name: Behind-the-Back Wrist Curl
equipmentNotes: A barbell held behind the hips.

name: Behind-the-Neck Press
equipmentNotes: Requires a squat/power rack with adjustable J-hooks and safety pins (bar un-racked at shoulder height rather than cleaned); needs sufficient overhead ceiling clearance for full bar extension; if performed seated, requires a vertical-backed bench (not an incline bench).

name: Belt Squat
equipmentNotes: A belt squat machine, or a dip belt and two raised platforms to stand on.

name: Bench Dip
equipmentNotes: A bench behind, and a second bench or the floor for the feet.

name: Bird Dog
equipmentNotes: Floor space; on hands and knees.

name: Block Pull
equipmentNotes: Requires a barbell plus a matched pair of fixed-height pulling blocks (wood, rubber, or urethane) placed under each end of the bar to set an elevated starting height; no rack or bench required. Chalk/straps commonly used as grip can become limiting.

name: Board Press
equipmentNotes: Requires a flat bench, power rack or bench station with safety pins/spotter arms, wood boards (commonly 2x6 lumber, ~1.5 inches thick each, stacked in sets of 1-4) or a comparable foam block, and a spotter or straps to hold the boards in place on the lifter's chest.

name: Bodyweight Squat
equipmentNotes: None. Floor space.

name: Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Press
equipmentNotes: Requires a single kettlebell held inverted by the handle; no rack, bench, or bar path hardware needed.

name: Box Jump
equipmentNotes: A box at a height you can land on with the hips above the knees.

name: Box Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a squat rack with adjustable safety pins and a sturdy flat squat box set to individualized depth; optional chalk, knee sleeves/wraps, belt.

name: Broad Jump
equipmentNotes: A runway with a soft landing surface.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a bench, box, or low rack pin (knee-to-mid-shin height) to elevate the rear foot, plus clear floor space front and back for a full split stance. Barbell version typically doesn't need a rack (stepped or cleaned into position). Non-slip flooring is important due to single-point front-foot base.

name: Cable Chest Press
equipmentNotes: A dual cable stack set at chest height.

name: Cable Crossover
equipmentNotes: A dual cable stack set high, with handles on both sides.

name: Cable Crunch
equipmentNotes: A high cable pulley with a rope, knelt beneath it.

name: Cable Curl
equipmentNotes: A low cable pulley with a straight or EZ bar.

name: Cable External Rotation
equipmentNotes: A cable stack set at elbow height; a towel under the elbow is common.

name: Cable Fly
equipmentNotes: Requires a dual-adjustable cable crossover tower with handle attachments, pulleys set at approximately shoulder height; needs clear floor space between towers for standing stance.

name: Cable Front Raise
equipmentNotes: A low cable pulley with a straight bar or single handle.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
equipmentNotes: Cable column or cable crossover tower with low pulley setting; requires an ankle cuff attachment (not a handle). No rack, bench, or bar needed. A stable handhold on the frame is used for balance.

name: Cable Hammer Curl
equipmentNotes: A low cable pulley with a rope attachment.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
equipmentNotes: A low cable pulley with a single handle.

name: Cable Lift
equipmentNotes: A low cable pulley with a rope or D-handle.

name: Cable Overhead Press
equipmentNotes: A cable stack set low, with a straight or rope handle.

name: Cable Pull-Through
equipmentNotes: A low cable pulley with a rope, faced away from the stack.

name: Cable Pullover
equipmentNotes: Cable station with adjustable pulley; straight bar, lat bar, or rope attachment; flat bench required only for lying low-pulley variation.

name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
equipmentNotes: A dual cable stack set at shoulder height or above.

name: Cable Shrug
equipmentNotes: A low cable pulley with a straight bar.

name: Cable Triceps Kickback
equipmentNotes: A low cable pulley with a single handle.

name: Cable Upright Row
equipmentNotes: A low cable pulley with a straight bar or rope.

name: Cable Woodchop
equipmentNotes: A high cable pulley with a rope or D-handle.

name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
equipmentNotes: A captain's chair with forearm pads.

name: Cat-Cow
equipmentNotes: Floor space; on hands and knees.

name: Chest Dip
equipmentNotes: Requires parallel dip bars or a dip station/rig attachment with adequate overhead and ground clearance; dip belt and plates or weight vest needed for added load; a step or box may help mounting. Rings can substitute but constitute a distinct, less stable variant.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
equipmentNotes: Two dumbbells and an incline bench set to about 30-45 degrees.

name: Chest-Supported Machine Row
equipmentNotes: A chest-supported row machine with a pad for the torso.

name: Chin-Up
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar with room to hang at full stretch.

name: Clamshell
equipmentNotes: Floor space; a mini band above the knees adds load.

name: Clean and Jerk
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Clean High Pull
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Clean Pull
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
equipmentNotes: Flat bench (0° incline) with a bench press rack/station or squat rack set up for bench; spotter or safety arms/pins recommended due to reduced bar stability and shortened triceps leverage with narrow grip. Can also be performed on a Smith machine as a fixed-bar-path variant.

name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
equipmentNotes: A lat pulldown station with a thigh pad.

name: Close-Grip Push-Up
equipmentNotes: Floor space; hands set inside shoulder width.

name: Concentration Curl
equipmentNotes: One dumbbell and a bench to sit on.

name: Conventional Deadlift
equipmentNotes: A barbell and plates that put the bar at standard height.

name: Copenhagen Plank
equipmentNotes: Requires a bench, box, or step to elevate and support the top leg, plus open floor space for the forearm-supported side-plank position. No rack or specialized equipment needed.

name: Cossack Squat
equipmentNotes: Floor space and hip range; a light kettlebell held at the chest adds load.

name: Couch Stretch
equipmentNotes: A wall or couch to set the back foot against, and a pad for the down knee.

name: Countermovement Jump
equipmentNotes: Floor space; a jump mat or Vertec if the height is being measured.

name: Cross-Body Hammer Curl
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells, curled across the torso.

name: Crunch
equipmentNotes: Floor space; lie face-up with knees bent.

name: Cuban Press
equipmentNotes: A pair of very light dumbbells or an empty bar.

name: Curtsy Lunge
equipmentNotes: Requires open floor space with lateral clearance for the diagonal cross-behind step; non-slip flooring recommended. Can be done bodyweight, dumbbell, kettlebell, or band; barbell back-racked possible but less common. Not suited to machine, cable, landmine, or sled.

name: Dead Bug
equipmentNotes: Floor space; lie face-up.

name: Dead Hang
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar with room to hang at full stretch.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
equipmentNotes: Requires a dedicated decline bench with ankle/foot-lock pads and an integrated head-end barbell support; standard adjustable safety pins don't align to the decline angle, so a spotter is the primary safety method.

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells and a decline bench.

name: Decline Push-Up
equipmentNotes: Requires a stable elevated surface for the feet (bench, step, plyo box, or sturdy chair, roughly knee-to-hip height), sufficient clear floor space for a full plank position, and a non-slip floor or mat under the hands. No rack, bench, or angled equipment needed.

name: Decline Sit-Up
equipmentNotes: A decline bench with foot rollers.

name: Deficit Deadlift
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a platform one to three inches high to stand on.

name: Deficit Push-Up
equipmentNotes: Pair of stable, equal-height elevation surfaces for hands (parallettes, push-up blocks, plates, or hex dumbbells); clear floor space with non-slip surface; no rack, bench, or rings required for standard version.

name: Deficit Reverse Lunge
equipmentNotes: Requires a stable elevated platform/box/plate stack of known, consistent height to stand on; sufficient clear floor space behind it for the stepping leg; non-slip flooring or platform edge; rack access if barbell-loaded.

name: Depth Jump
equipmentNotes: Plyometric box(es) of fixed, known height (commonly 12–24 in / 30–60 cm); adequate ceiling clearance for vertical jump; firm non-compliant landing surface; open floor space for landing and re-jump; optional contact mat or force plate/timing system to measure ground contact time and reactive strength index. No rack or spotter needed.

name: Diamond Push-Up
equipmentNotes: Floor space; hands together under the chest.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
equipmentNotes: A donkey calf raise machine, or a partner and a raised step.

name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
equipmentNotes: Two kettlebells racked on the forearms.

name: Drag Curl
equipmentNotes: A barbell dragged up the torso with the elbows travelling back.

name: Dragon Flag
equipmentNotes: A bench to hold behind the head, or a sturdy upright.

name: Drop Landing
equipmentNotes: A low box to step off; the drill is the landing, not the jump.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells and a flat bench.

name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a stable elevated surface (bench, box, or step) for the rear foot, set at knee-to-mid-shin height; sufficient open floor space in front for the working-leg stance and safe dumbbell drop; non-slip floor under the front foot. No rack, safeties, or bench-angle requirement needed since load is hand-held.

name: Dumbbell Curl
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells.

name: Dumbbell External Rotation
equipmentNotes: One light dumbbell; usually done side-lying or standing with the elbow pinned.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
equipmentNotes: Performed lying supine on open floor; no bench, rack, or spotter required since the floor limits range of motion and acts as a safety stop. Requires clear floor space and a method to bring dumbbells into starting position (e.g., kicking them up from a seated position) since there is no rack to lift from.

name: Dumbbell Fly
equipmentNotes: Requires a flat bench (0°, not a rack), sufficient lateral/overhead clearance for full arm abduction, and a dumbbell pair/rack for loading.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
equipmentNotes: A pair of light dumbbells.

name: Dumbbell Jump Squat
equipmentNotes: Open, unobstructed floor space with adequate ceiling height for vertical displacement; non-slip, shock-tolerant flooring to handle landing impact. No rack, bench, or safeties required.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
equipmentNotes: A pair of light dumbbells.

name: Dumbbell Lunge
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells and room to step.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
equipmentNotes: One dumbbell and a flat bench, or a bench taken across the back.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells.

name: Dumbbell Row
equipmentNotes: One dumbbell and a bench to brace the free hand and knee.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells; done seated with a back support or standing.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
equipmentNotes: A pair of heavy dumbbells.

name: Dumbbell Skullcrusher
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells and a flat bench.

name: Dumbbell Snatch
equipmentNotes: One dumbbell and room to stand tall overhead.

name: Dumbbell Squat
equipmentNotes: Pair of dumbbells spanning an adequate weight range; open, unobstructed floor space to lift dumbbells into starting position and lower them at end of set; no rack, safeties, or bench required.

name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
equipmentNotes: Requires a pair of dumbbells (hex-shaped preferred for flat mating faces) and a flat bench. No rack, safeties, or spotter needed.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up
equipmentNotes: Requires a stable, non-slip step/box/bench set near knee height, with adequate floor clearance front and back, plus a pair of dumbbells; no rack or bench angle needed.

name: Dumbbell Swing
equipmentNotes: One dumbbell held at the end, with clear space fore and aft.

name: Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
equipmentNotes: One light dumbbell and a bench to brace on.

name: Dumbbell Upright Row
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells and a bench to rest the forearms on.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
equipmentNotes: An EZ-curl bar, which spares the wrists.

name: EZ-Bar Preacher Curl
equipmentNotes: A preacher bench and an EZ-curl bar.

name: EZ-Bar Skullcrusher
equipmentNotes: An EZ-curl bar and a flat bench.

name: Face Pull
equipmentNotes: A cable stack set at face height with a rope attachment.

name: Farmer's Walk
equipmentNotes: Farmer's handles, heavy dumbbells or kettlebells, and a lane to walk.

name: Fire Hydrant
equipmentNotes: Floor space; on hands and knees.

name: Floor Press
equipmentNotes: Performed lying on a clear flat floor, typically inside a power rack with safety pins/J-hooks set low to rack/unrack the bar at floor height; no bench used; spotter recommended for heavy loads.

name: Forward Lunge
equipmentNotes: Floor space; dumbbells or a barbell add load.

name: Frog Pump
equipmentNotes: Performed supine on a mat or floor; optional light barbell, dumbbell, or kettlebell across the hips, or a mini resistance band around the knees/thighs. No rack, bench, or machine required.

name: Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a low, stable elevation platform (plate, low box, or step) for the front foot, and adequate clear floor space with good traction for a split stance. If barbell-loaded, rack access needed for un-racking/re-racking; no safety pins needed mid-set. No bench, rings, or cable apparatus required.

name: Front Rack Carry
equipmentNotes: Two kettlebells racked on the forearms.

name: Front Squat
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a rack; needs wrist and thoracic range to hold the rack position.

name: Glute Bridge
equipmentNotes: Flat floor or mat; no bench or rack needed. If loaded, a barbell pad or folded mat across the hip crease; bar travels only a few inches so no rack/spotter arms required.

name: Glute Bridge March
equipmentNotes: Floor space; lie face-up with the feet planted.

name: Glute Drive Machine
equipmentNotes: A glute drive machine with a back pad and a foot platform, pin- or plate-loaded.

name: Glute-Ham Raise
equipmentNotes: A glute-ham developer; the pad support is what separates it from a Nordic curl.

name: Glute Kickback Machine
equipmentNotes: A standing glute kickback machine with an ankle or foot pad.

name: Goblet Squat
equipmentNotes: Open floor space only; no rack, safeties, bench, or rig required. Needs a dumbbell or kettlebell and clearance for full squat depth.

name: Good Morning
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a rack; start light, the leverage is unforgiving.

name: Gorilla Row
equipmentNotes: Two kettlebells set on the floor between the feet.

name: Hack Squat Machine
equipmentNotes: An angled hack squat sled with shoulder pads.

name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Press
equipmentNotes: A barbell in a landmine sleeve or wedged in a corner; a pad for the down knee.

name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press
equipmentNotes: A cable stack at chest height; a pad for the down knee.

name: Hammer Curl
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells held neutral.

name: Hammer Strength Chest Press
equipmentNotes: Plate-loaded, independently pivoting (iso-lateral) linkage arms; adjustable seat; self-supporting unit requiring no rack, spotter, or bench incline.

name: Hammer Strength Row
equipmentNotes: A plate-loaded iso-lateral row machine with independent arms.

name: Handstand Push-Up
equipmentNotes: A clear wall to kick up against, or parallettes for added depth.

name: Hang Clean
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Hang Power Clean
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Hang Snatch
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar.

name: Hatfield Squat
equipmentNotes: Performed in a power rack or squat stand with adjustable uprights/pins positioned near chest/shoulder height for hand support, typically paired with a Safety Squat Bar; requires safety pins/arms set at an appropriate catch height.

name: High Bar Back Squat
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a rack with safeties; the bar sits on the traps.

name: High-to-Low Cable Fly
equipmentNotes: A dual cable stack set above shoulder height.

name: Hill Sprint
equipmentNotes: A hill with a consistent grade and safe footing.

name: Hip Flexor March
equipmentNotes: Floor space; a band around the feet adds load.

name: Hip Thrust Machine
equipmentNotes: Dedicated hip thrust machine (plate-loaded pin or weight stack) with padded hip/shin contact point and back pad/platform for shoulders; requires floor clearance for plate loading if applicable; no squat rack, bench, barbell, or dumbbells needed.

name: Hollow Body Hold
equipmentNotes: Floor space; lie face-up.

name: Horizontal Leg Press
equipmentNotes: Self-contained horizontal leg press unit (plate-loaded carriage or selectorized stack) with footplate and backrest; no rack, safeties, or bench required; needs floor clearance behind the unit for carriage travel and plate loading.

name: Hurdle Hop
equipmentNotes: Low hurdles or cones set in a line.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
equipmentNotes: Requires a dedicated incline bench set at 30–45°, and a rack or incline-press station with safety pins/spotter arms positioned for the angled bar path; needs extra overhead clearance compared to flat bench.

name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
equipmentNotes: Adjustable bench set to roughly 30–45° incline; requires floor clearance and stable seated position to kick dumbbells into place; dumbbell rack nearby for handoff; side clearance needed to drop dumbbells safely if a rep is failed.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells and a bench set to about 45-60 degrees.

name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
equipmentNotes: Adjustable incline bench set to roughly 30–45°; requires clear lateral space on both sides of the bench beyond its width for arm travel at the bottom of the rep. No rack, safeties, or spotter required.

name: Incline Machine Chest Press
equipmentNotes: An incline chest press machine, pin- or plate-loaded.

name: Incline Push-Up
equipmentNotes: A bench, box or bar to put the hands on; the higher the hands, the easier.

name: Inverted Row
equipmentNotes: A bar in a rack or a Smith machine set at waist height.

name: Iso-Lateral Chest Press
equipmentNotes: A plate-loaded chest press with independent arms.

name: Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press
equipmentNotes: A plate-loaded shoulder press with independent arms, so neither side can carry the other.

name: Jefferson Curl
equipmentNotes: Performed with barbell, dumbbell, kettlebell, or weight plate while standing on an elevated surface such as a plyometric box to allow full spinal flexion range of motion.

name: JM Press
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a flat bench; a hybrid of a close-grip press and a skullcrusher.

name: Jump Squat
equipmentNotes: Can be loaded with bodyweight only, barbell (back or trap-bar position), dumbbells, kettlebell, or weighted vest; requires vertical clearance and impact-tolerant, non-slip flooring for repeated landings.

name: Kettlebell Clean
equipmentNotes: One kettlebell; the rack position lands on the forearm.

name: Kettlebell Front Squat
equipmentNotes: No rack, bench, or barbell safety equipment needed; requires open floor space with overhead clearance to clean/press kettlebell(s) into rack position and a stable stance footprint.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
equipmentNotes: One or two kettlebells racked on the forearm.

name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
equipmentNotes: Open floor space with clearance to hinge and lower bell(s) toward mid-shin; level, non-slip floor; chalk or grip aids for heavier loads. No rack, bench, or spotter needed.

name: Kettlebell Row
equipmentNotes: One kettlebell and a bench or rack to brace against.

name: Kettlebell Snatch
equipmentNotes: One kettlebell and overhead clearance.

name: Kettlebell Swing
equipmentNotes: One kettlebell and clear space in front and behind.

name: Kneeling Cable Pulldown
equipmentNotes: A high cable pulley; kneel far enough back to keep the line of pull overhead.

name: Landmine Chest Press
equipmentNotes: A barbell in a landmine sleeve or wedged in a corner, pressed from the shoulder.

name: Landmine Press
equipmentNotes: Requires a landmine attachment (sleeve) bolted to a rack/plate or a wall/floor corner to wedge the bar end; open floor space needed for the bar's arcing path. No rack, bench, or safeties required.

name: Landmine Romanian Deadlift
equipmentNotes: Requires a landmine attachment (angled floor sleeve/pivot, free-standing unit or rack-insert sleeve) and open floor clearance for the bar's arcing path; no bench, rack safeties, or rings needed.

name: Landmine Rotation
equipmentNotes: A barbell in a landmine sleeve, held at chest height.

name: Landmine Row
equipmentNotes: A barbell in a landmine sleeve or wedged in a corner, with a V-handle.

name: Landmine Squat
equipmentNotes: A barbell in a landmine sleeve, held at the chest.

name: Lat Pulldown
equipmentNotes: A lat pulldown station with a thigh pad.

name: Lateral Band Walk
equipmentNotes: A mini band around the ankles, knees or feet; a mini-squat stance raises activation.

name: Lateral Bound
equipmentNotes: Open floor with room to travel sideways.

name: Lateral Lunge
equipmentNotes: Bodyweight, dumbbells, kettlebells, or back-racked barbell; requires open unobstructed floor space to each side for a wide lateral step; barbell version requires squat-rack setup.

name: Lateral Step-Up
equipmentNotes: Requires a stable, non-slip box/bench/step (roughly 6–18 in / 15–45 cm) allowing full hip and knee extension at the top, plus sufficient lateral floor clearance on both sides of the box for the sideways stepping motion. No rack, angled bench, or rings needed.

name: Leaning Lateral Raise
equipmentNotes: A dumbbell and an upright to hang off with the free hand.

name: Leg Extension
equipmentNotes: A leg extension machine with a shin pad.

name: Leg Press
equipmentNotes: A 45-degree leg press sled.

name: Leg Press Calf Raise
equipmentNotes: A leg press with the feet set low on the platform.

name: Long-Lever Plank
equipmentNotes: Floor space; elbows set forward of the shoulders.

name: Low Bar Back Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a squat rack or power rack with adjustable J-hooks and safety pins/straps set to the lifter's low-bar unracking height; standard Olympic barbell and plates; stable non-compliant floor; clear rack footprint and walk-out space.

name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
equipmentNotes: Dual-adjustable-pulley cable crossover station (functional trainer) with both pulleys set to lowest position; D-handle attachments on each side; open floor space between towers for a full low-to-high arc; stable non-slip standing surface (no bench/rack required).

name: Lu Raise
equipmentNotes: A pair of very light dumbbells; the arms finish overhead.

name: Lying Leg Curl
equipmentNotes: A lying leg curl machine with an ankle pad.

name: Lying Leg Raise
equipmentNotes: Floor space; lie face-up.

name: Lying Plate Lateral Neck Flexion
equipmentNotes: On one side on a bench, head off the end, a towel and plate on the upper side of the head; raise the head toward the shoulder, no shrug or turn, then switch sides.

name: Lying Plate Neck Extension
equipmentNotes: Face down on a bench, head off the end, a towel and plate on the back of the head held in place with both hands; raise the head into extension and lower under control.

name: Lying Plate Neck Flexion
aliases: Weight Plate Lying Face Up Neck Resistance
equipmentNotes: Face up on a flat bench, head just off the end, a folded towel on the forehead and a plate held over it; tuck the chin and curl the head up without lifting the shoulders.

name: Machine Chest Press
equipmentNotes: A seated chest-press machine, pin-loaded or plate-loaded.

name: Machine Crunch
equipmentNotes: A seated abdominal crunch machine.

name: Machine Fly
equipmentNotes: A pec deck or fly machine with arm pads or handles.

name: Machine Lateral Raise
equipmentNotes: A seated lateral-raise machine with pads on the outer arms.

name: Machine Preacher Curl
equipmentNotes: A seated biceps curl machine with an arm pad.

name: Machine Pulldown
equipmentNotes: A seated pulldown machine, pin-loaded or plate-loaded.

name: Machine Rear Delt Fly
equipmentNotes: A pec deck set to run in reverse, or a dedicated rear-delt machine.

name: Machine Row
equipmentNotes: A seated row machine, pin-loaded or plate-loaded.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
equipmentNotes: A seated shoulder-press machine, pin-loaded or plate-loaded.

name: Machine Shrug
equipmentNotes: A shrug machine, or a Smith machine.

name: Machine Triceps Extension
equipmentNotes: A seated triceps extension machine.

name: McGill Curl-Up
equipmentNotes: Floor space. Hands go under the lumbar spine to hold its natural curve, and one knee stays bent; short holds rather than reps.

name: Meadows Row
equipmentNotes: A barbell in a landmine, gripped at the sleeve end and rowed from the side.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
equipmentNotes: A medicine ball and a wall or partner to throw at.

name: Medicine Ball Slam
equipmentNotes: A non-bouncing slam ball and a floor that will take it.

name: Muscle Snatch
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Neck Harness Extension
equipmentNotes: A head harness with a plate or chain hanging from it, torso braced on the thighs or a bench; extend the head against the load. EMG shows little upper-trapezius work.

name: Neck Machine Extension
equipmentNotes: A 4-way neck machine, seated facing away, the back of the head on the pad; press the head back into extension against the load.

name: Neck Machine Flexion
equipmentNotes: A 4-way neck machine, seated facing the head pad, forehead on the pad; bring the chin toward the chest against the stack or plates.

name: Neck Machine Lateral Flexion
equipmentNotes: A 4-way neck machine, seated side-on, the side of the head on the pad; bend the head toward the shoulder, shoulders down, no rotation; both sides.

name: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Press
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells held palms-in, which is often easier on the shoulder.

name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
equipmentNotes: A lat pulldown station with a thigh pad.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar with parallel handles.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
equipmentNotes: Requires an ankle-anchoring apparatus (dedicated Nordic bench/board, GHD footplate, fixed low bar, or partner holding ankles), a padded mat/knee pad, and clear floor space in front of the lifter to fall forward safely (crash pad or spotter recommended for beginners). Optional: strap-force dynamometer (e.g., NordBord) for measuring eccentric force output; optional weight vest for added resistance.

name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
equipmentNotes: A low or high cable pulley, faced away from the stack.

name: Overhead Carry
equipmentNotes: One or two implements held locked out overhead.

name: Overhead Medicine Ball Throw
equipmentNotes: A medicine ball and open space behind or in front.

name: Overhead Press
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a rack set at upper-chest height, or the floor to clean it from.

name: Overhead Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a squat rack or power rack with adjustable J-hooks/pins for snatch-grip-height bar takeout, sufficient overhead ceiling clearance for full lockout, and safety arms/pins or a bumper-plate platform since missed lifts are typically dropped rather than recovered to the shoulders.

name: Pallof Press
equipmentNotes: A cable stack at chest height, stood side-on.

name: Pause Bench Press
equipmentNotes: Flat bench with rack or dedicated bench station; adjustable J-hooks; safety arms/pins set at chest height required since a failed paused rep has no bounce-assisted bail-out.

name: Pause Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a squat/power rack with safety pins or spotter arms set near bottom depth for fall-safety during the static hold, J-hooks set to shoulder height, and a standardized method (count, cue, or timer) to fix pause duration.

name: Pec Deck
equipmentNotes: A pec deck with forearm pads.

name: Pendlay Row
equipmentNotes: A barbell and plates tall enough to reset on the floor each rep.

name: Pendulum Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a dedicated plate-loaded Pendulum Squat machine with a pivoting/arcing loading arm, shoulder or chest pads, and an angled footplate; no barbell, rack, or bench needed, but clearance for the arc of the pendulum arm is required.

name: Pike Push-Up
equipmentNotes: Floor space; a box or bench under the feet raises the load.

name: Pin Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a power rack (squat rack) with adjustable pins/safety bars set at a specific height to support the bar at or near bottom squat depth; no bench or other specialized equipment needed.

name: Pistol Squat
equipmentNotes: No rack/bar required; open floor space needed for extended leg range of motion on a stable non-slip surface. Optional: low box/bench for depth regulation or assistance, single dumbbell/kettlebell for added load, or overhead/low anchor point for band-assisted variations.

name: Plank
equipmentNotes: Floor space; forearms down.

name: Plate Front Raise
equipmentNotes: A single weight plate held at the edges.

name: Plate Pinch
equipmentNotes: Two smooth weight plates pinched between thumb and fingers.

name: Plyometric Push-Up
equipmentNotes: Floor space with some give; the hands leave the ground.

name: Pogo Hop
equipmentNotes: Open floor space with firm, non-slip footing required; no rack/bench/bar needed. Optional: contact mat or force plate for ground-contact time/RSI measurement; weighted vest for loaded progression.

name: Power Clean
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Power Snatch
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Preacher Curl
equipmentNotes: A preacher bench and an EZ or straight bar.

name: Prisoner Squat
equipmentNotes: No equipment required; open floor space only. Bodyweight only, no external load.

name: Prone T Raise
equipmentNotes: A bench or the floor to lie face-down on.

name: Prone W Raise
equipmentNotes: A bench or the floor to lie face-down on.

name: Prone Y Raise
equipmentNotes: A bench or the floor to lie face-down on; very light dumbbells or plates are optional.

name: Pull-Up
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar with room to hang at full stretch.

name: Pullover Machine
equipmentNotes: A seated pullover machine with elbow pads.

name: Push Jerk
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Push Press
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a rack set at upper-chest height.

name: Push-Up
equipmentNotes: None. Floor space.

name: Rack Pull
equipmentNotes: Requires a power rack or squat rack with pins set at a fixed height (commonly below-knee to mid-thigh), or equivalent lifting blocks/boxes, plus barbell and weight plates. Chalk/straps optional for grip.

name: Rear Delt Fly
equipmentNotes: A pair of light dumbbells; a bench to brace the chest is optional.

name: Renegade Row
equipmentNotes: Two hex dumbbells that will not roll, on a non-slip floor.

name: Reverse Crunch
equipmentNotes: Floor space; lie face-up.

name: Reverse Curl
equipmentNotes: A straight or EZ bar taken overhand.

name: Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldown
equipmentNotes: A lat pulldown station with a thigh pad.

name: Reverse Hyperextension
equipmentNotes: Requires a dedicated reverse hyperextension (pendulum) machine with hip pad, swinging pendulum arm, weight horn/pin stack, and torso-stabilizing handles; cannot be substituted with a bench, back-extension bench, or rack.

name: Reverse Lunge
equipmentNotes: Can be loaded with bodyweight, dumbbells (goblet-held or one in each hand/suitcase), kettlebells (goblet or offset/rack), or barbell (back or front rack). Landmine and band loading exist but are less standard; cable and sled loading are not conventional for this exercise.

name: Reverse Wrist Curl
equipmentNotes: Light dumbbells or a bar, forearms braced palm-down.

name: Ring Dip
equipmentNotes: Gymnastic rings hung with room to lock out below them.

name: Ring Push-Up
equipmentNotes: Requires a pair of gymnastic rings mounted on adjustable-height straps from a rig, pull-up station, or ceiling mount, with sufficient overhead clearance and floor space for a full push-up body-length position and free swing/rotation of the rings without obstruction.

name: Ring Row
equipmentNotes: Gymnastic rings hung at waist to chest height.

name: RKC Plank
equipmentNotes: Floor space; the whole body braced hard for short holds.

name: Romanian Deadlift
equipmentNotes: A barbell, taken from a rack or from the top of a deadlift.

name: Rope Overhead Triceps Extension
equipmentNotes: A cable pulley with a rope, faced away from the stack.

name: Rope Triceps Pushdown
equipmentNotes: A high cable pulley with a rope attachment.

name: Rotary Torso Machine
equipmentNotes: A seated rotary torso machine with a fixed pelvis pad.

name: Rotational Medicine Ball Throw
equipmentNotes: A medicine ball and a solid wall to throw against.

name: Russian Twist
equipmentNotes: Floor space; a plate or medicine ball adds load.

name: Safety Bar Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a specialized safety squat bar (cambered sleeves, padded shoulder yoke, forward-projecting handles) loaded with standard plates, used in a squat/power rack with safety pins or spotter arms set to an appropriate catch height. Needs adequate overhead clearance for the bar's camber when racking/unracking, and a flat, stable platform for stance. No bench, incline, or rings needed.

name: Scapular Pull-Up
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar with room to hang at full stretch.

name: Scapular Push-Up
equipmentNotes: Floor space; can be done against a wall to reduce load.

name: Seal Row
equipmentNotes: A barbell and a bench raised high enough for the plates to clear the floor.

name: Seated Barbell Overhead Press
equipmentNotes: Requires a rack or power cage with adjustable safety pins/hooks at shoulder height, or a dedicated seated shoulder-press station; seat must have a vertical (~90°) back support rather than an incline bench; standard bar, plates, and collars; adequate overhead clearance needed for lockout.

name: Seated Cable Row
equipmentNotes: A seated cable row station with a foot plate and a V-handle.

name: Seated Calf Raise
equipmentNotes: A seated calf raise machine with a thigh pad; the bent knee shifts the work to the soleus.

name: Seated Dip Machine
equipmentNotes: A seated dip machine with handles at the hips.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells and a bench with an upright back.

name: Seated Good Morning
equipmentNotes: Requires a flat or adjustable bench positioned inside a power rack with adjustable safety hooks/pins set at standing-bar-on-traps height so the bar can be racked/unracked while seated. Barbell pad common but not required. May be substituted with a Smith machine or dedicated seated good-morning/back-extension machine.

name: Seated Hip Abduction Machine
equipmentNotes: A seated abduction machine with pads outside the knees.

name: Seated Hip Adduction Machine
equipmentNotes: Dedicated seated hip adduction machine: fixed seat with back support, pin-loaded weight stack, pivoting lever arms with thigh/knee pads, adjustable start-position lever to set beginning abduction angle/range of motion. No rack, bench, or additional apparatus required.

name: Seated Leg Curl
equipmentNotes: A seated leg curl machine with a thigh pad.

name: Short Foot Drill
equipmentNotes: Bare feet on a flat floor. The metatarsal heads draw toward the heel without the toes curling.

name: Shrimp Squat
equipmentNotes: No equipment required; needs clear floor space and a non-slip surface/mat. Optional wall/pole/TRX/band for balance assistance; optional dumbbell or weight vest for loaded progressions.

name: Side Bend
equipmentNotes: One dumbbell held at the side.

name: Side Plank
equipmentNotes: Floor space; one forearm down.

name: Single-Arm Cable Chest Press
equipmentNotes: A cable stack at chest height with one handle.

name: Single-Arm Cable Row
equipmentNotes: A cable stack set at waist height with a single handle.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Press
equipmentNotes: One dumbbell; the free side has to resist the lean.

name: Single-Arm Farmer's Walk
equipmentNotes: One heavy implement and a lane to walk.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
equipmentNotes: Open floor space with headroom and a clear front-and-back arc for the kettlebell's swing path; non-slip floor surface; lateral clearance for single-arm sway/rotation. No rack or bench required.

name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
equipmentNotes: A high cable pulley with a single handle.

name: Single-Leg Balance
equipmentNotes: Flat floor; no equipment.

name: Single-Leg Bound
equipmentNotes: A runway with room to travel forward.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
equipmentNotes: A step to drop the heel below; a dumbbell in one hand adds load.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
equipmentNotes: A bench to set the shoulders on; a dumbbell across the hip adds load.

name: Single-Leg Leg Extension
equipmentNotes: A leg extension machine, one leg at a time.

name: Single-Leg Leg Press
equipmentNotes: A leg press sled, one foot centred on the platform.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
equipmentNotes: One dumbbell or kettlebell and something to touch for balance.

name: Single-Leg Stand with Eyes Closed
equipmentNotes: Flat floor and something to catch yourself on.

name: Sissy Squat
equipmentNotes: Bodyweight by default; can be loaded with a dumbbell/plate at the chest or a weight vest; can be performed on a dedicated sissy squat bench/machine with ankle-lock and knee pad, or freestanding while holding a fixed support (squat rack upright, pole, TRX strap, or partner's hands) for balance.

name: Skater Squat
equipmentNotes: Low box/plate/block under working foot for deficit; soft pad or block to cushion rear knee descent; optional wall or support for balance during regression.

name: Skullcrusher
equipmentNotes: An EZ or straight bar and a flat bench.

name: Sled Drag
equipmentNotes: A drag sled with a harness or straps.

name: Sled Push
equipmentNotes: A push sled and a lane with enough traction.

name: Sled Row
equipmentNotes: A sled, a rope or straps, and a lane to pull along.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
equipmentNotes: Requires a Smith machine with a fixed vertical or slightly angled rail-guided bar and integrated hook/stop pins (built-in safeties, no spotter required), plus a flat bench positioned under the bar at correct height/alignment.

name: Smith Machine Incline Press
equipmentNotes: A Smith machine and an incline bench set to about 30-45 degrees.

name: Smith Machine Overhead Press
equipmentNotes: A Smith machine and an upright bench, or done standing.

name: Smith Machine Row
equipmentNotes: A Smith machine with the bar set low. The fixed path takes the stabilisers out.

name: Smith Machine Squat
equipmentNotes: A Smith machine; the fixed path sets the stance for you.

name: Snatch Balance
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift
equipmentNotes: A barbell taken at the wide snatch grip; straps are common.

name: Snatch Pull
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform.

name: Spider Curl
equipmentNotes: An incline bench to lie face-down on, with dumbbells or an EZ bar.

name: Split Jerk
equipmentNotes: A barbell, bumper plates and a platform; the bar is dropped from overhead.

name: Split Squat
equipmentNotes: Commonly loaded with bodyweight, dumbbells (goblet or suitcase), kettlebell, barbell (back- or front-rack), landmine, or Smith machine; no standard cable or band-primary loading mode.

name: Spoto Press
equipmentNotes: Power rack or bench station with J-hooks/uprights, flat bench, safety arms/pins or spotter recommended; sufficient clearance to lower bar to 1-2 inches above sternum without resting on chest.

name: Standing Calf Raise
equipmentNotes: A standing calf raise machine, or a step and a loaded bar.

name: Standing Hip Abduction
equipmentNotes: Low cable pulley with ankle-cuff attachment, standing hip-abduction machine, or band anchored at floor/post level; requires stable standing surface and support (handle/frame/wall) for balance on the stance leg. No rack, bench, or barbell needed.

name: Standing Leg Curl
equipmentNotes: A standing leg curl machine, one leg at a time.

name: Step-Down
equipmentNotes: Adjustable box/step (~10-30 cm / 4-12 in) with stable, non-slip top; clear floor space in front for the free leg to descend; optional dumbbell rack if loaded with dumbbells.

name: Step-Up
equipmentNotes: Sturdy, non-slip, fixed-height platform/box/bench sized so the working knee is near ~90° at the top. If barbell-loaded, needs a rack or clean-to-shoulders access; otherwise just floor clearance around the platform for stride length and storage of dumbbells/kettlebells nearby. No rack-with-safeties or angled bench required.

name: Stiff-Legged Deadlift
equipmentNotes: Requires flat, stable, non-give platform or deadlift platform with floor-start/reset each rep; adequate overhead/floor clearance; standard calibrated or bumper plates to maintain consistent bar height; chalk or straps for grip. No rack, bench, or incline surface needed.

name: Stir the Pot
equipmentNotes: A stability ball to plank on with the forearms.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
equipmentNotes: A high cable pulley with a straight bar or rope.

name: Suitcase Carry
equipmentNotes: One dumbbell or kettlebell, carried at one side.

name: Suitcase Deadlift
equipmentNotes: One heavy dumbbell or kettlebell set beside the foot.

name: Sumo Deadlift
equipmentNotes: Barbell, calibrated plates, flat non-slip lifting platform/deadlift mat; no rack or bench needed; requires wider floor clearance for sumo stance.

name: Supine 90/90 Breathing
equipmentNotes: Floor space and a box or wall to rest the lower legs on at right angles; a slow nasal inhale against a longer exhale.

name: Svend Press
equipmentNotes: Two weight plates pressed together between the palms.

name: T-Bar Row
equipmentNotes: A T-bar row station, or a barbell in a landmine with a V-handle.

name: Tate Press
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells and a flat bench.

name: Thoracic Rotation
equipmentNotes: Floor space; done side-lying or in a quadruped position.

name: Thruster
equipmentNotes: A barbell taken from the front rack.

name: Tibialis Raise
equipmentNotes: A wall to lean against, or a tib bar for load.

name: Toe Walk
equipmentNotes: Open floor to walk on the balls of the feet.

name: Toe Yoga
equipmentNotes: Bare feet on a flat floor; the big toe and the lesser toes lift independently.

name: Toes-to-Bar
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar with room to swing.

name: Towel Hang
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar and one or two towels thrown over it.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
equipmentNotes: Requires a trap/hex bar implement (not interchangeable with a straight barbell); open floor space, no rack or bench needed; standard plates, ideally bumper plates; lifting platform or impact-rated flooring recommended.

name: Trap Bar Shrug
equipmentNotes: A trap bar.

name: Triceps Pushdown
equipmentNotes: A high cable pulley with a straight or angled bar.

name: TRX Fallout
equipmentNotes: A suspension trainer anchored overhead; the further forward the feet, the harder it gets.

name: TRX Hamstring Curl
equipmentNotes: A suspension trainer anchored overhead, with the heels in the foot cradles.

name: TRX Pistol Squat
equipmentNotes: A suspension trainer anchored overhead to take some of the load through the hands.

name: TRX Push-Up
equipmentNotes: A suspension trainer anchored overhead; foot position sets the load.

name: TRX Row
equipmentNotes: A suspension trainer anchored overhead; foot position sets the load.

name: Tuck Jump
equipmentNotes: Floor space with some give underfoot.

name: Turkish Get-Up
equipmentNotes: One kettlebell and floor space to stand up and lie back down.

name: Upright Row
equipmentNotes: A barbell or EZ-bar.

name: V-Squat Machine
equipmentNotes: A V-squat sled with shoulder pads.

name: V-Up
equipmentNotes: Floor space; lie face-up.

name: Walking Lunge
equipmentNotes: A lane to travel down; dumbbells or a barbell add load.

name: Wall Sit
equipmentNotes: Flat, sturdy vertical wall with clear floor space for foot placement; optional dumbbell/plate/weight vest for loaded progression; stopwatch/timer to track hold duration.

name: Wall Slide
equipmentNotes: A flat wall; a foam roller or towel under the forearms is optional.

name: Weighted Pull-Up
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar plus a dip belt, weight vest or dumbbell between the feet.

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
equipmentNotes: A lat pulldown station with a thigh pad.

name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
equipmentNotes: A pull-up bar with room to hang at full stretch.

name: Wide-Grip Push-Up
equipmentNotes: Floor space; hands set wide.

name: Wide-Grip Seated Cable Row
equipmentNotes: A seated cable row station with a long straight bar.

name: World's Greatest Stretch
equipmentNotes: Floor space. It asks for hip and thoracic range most beginners do not have yet.

name: Wrist Roller
equipmentNotes: A roller handle with a cord and a hanging weight.

name: Yates Row
equipmentNotes: A barbell, taken with an underhand grip at a steeper torso angle.

name: Yoke Walk
equipmentNotes: A loaded yoke and a flat lane.

name: Z Press
equipmentNotes: Requires open floor space to sit with legs fully extended; barbell typically set up via power rack safety pins/spotter arms lowered to seated-shoulder height, or dumbbells/kettlebells positioned from the floor. No bench or back support used.

name: Zercher Squat
equipmentNotes: Requires a rack or squat stand with J-hooks set low (around elbow height), or ability to deadlift the bar into position from the floor if no low rack is available. Typically requires supplementary padding (thick bar pad, towel, or Airex pad) around the bar to reduce elbow-crease/bicep bruising. Needs open floor space to stand and walk the bar out.

name: Zottman Curl
equipmentNotes: A pair of dumbbells; the grip turns over at the top.
